title: Golden test vectors for Cyrillic ↔ Latin scheme from open authoritative examples
context: Golden test vectors are curated input/output pairs from open authoritative sources (UNGEGN sample word lists, PD corpora, openly-licensed reference materials). They are the most readable proof of correctness and catch specific known-hard cases. All examples must be neutral/PD text — no real personal names or identifiable individuals. Vectors must be sourced from the provenance allow-list; their origin is recorded per entry.
objective: Create at least 50 golden test vector pairs for the Cyrillic ↔ Latin (cyrl-latn-iso9a) scheme, sourced from open/PD authoritative examples, stored in data/vectors/cyrl-latn-iso9a/ and validated by the test harness. Cover: basic character mapping, uppercase/lowercase pairs, combining marks, multi-character grapheme clusters, digits, punctuation passthrough, and foreign-text passthrough.
acceptanceCriteria: data/vectors/cyrl-latn-iso9a/ contains >= 50 forward+inverse test vector pairs in the harness-expected format
Each vector records its source (provenance reference from the allow-list) and is neutral/PD text only — no real personal names or identifiable individuals

Vectors cover: all basic Cyrillic letter mappings (upper and lower), combining-mark edge cases, multi-character grapheme clusters, Cyrillic digits, punctuation and whitespace passthrough, and foreign-text passthrough
Known hard cases are explicitly represented: NFC vs NFD input normalization, Cyrillic/Latin homoglyphs, and any context-sensitive rules in the scheme
All vectors pass the harness golden-vector runner in CI (reverse(forward(s)) == NFC(s) for each pair)
Vector file(s) validate against a simple schema (id, input, expectedForward, expectedInverse, source, notes?) and are readable as YAML or JSON
resources: PLAN.md — Reversibility (golden vectors as proof method); hard-case test inventory (Appendix A)
UNGEGN sample word lists for geographical names (open/PD)
output: data/vectors/cyrl-latn-iso9a/ directory with >= 50 vector entries (YAML or JSON) and a provenance attribution file
